scope.statement: ONE downstream Hall accelerator reference, identical in hall_only, rf_hall and ecr_hall, so that the RF/ECR comparison changes only the pre-ionization method upstream of the Hall inlet plane HALL_INLET_Z0.
scope.block: Ionization/discharge -> acceleration/thrust block of the RFP architecture (CLAUDE.md 'Next work' 1, Scope). Nothing here reaches upstream into the intake, filter, compressor, gas chambers or valves; those deliver the feed state at IF-A5/IF-X2.
scope.own_thruster_not_p5: This is the interface of Vyovrinda's own thruster. P5 (and ECHT) geometry, B(z) files and coil settings are evidence about other hardware and are never Vyovrinda design values (forbidden_value_sources).
scope.no_performance_claims: No Hall performance number is predicted or implied. The credible transport set is empty (gate 3 FAIL); every value that would need an admitted closure or hardware is TBD.
scope.no_winner: No architecture is ranked, preferred or eliminated here. Eliminations happen only in the comparison harness through explicit hard-gate logic with the evidence class that supports them.
scope.not_wired: Pure data and documentation. Not imported by abep_sim/archengine.py or any existing module; goldens do not move.

channel_mean_radius_m.requires: TBD — requires a Vyovrinda thruster design release (drawing id, revision, sha256).

sizing_relations.relation: Annular channel cross-section A = (pi/4)(d_ext^2 - d_int^2) = pi d h (d mean diameter, h width).
sizing_relations.locator: SRC-DM2008 Eq. (2.8), p. 7; HallThruster.jl src/thruster/geometry.jl channel_area

sizing_relations.relation: Melikov-Morozov criterion lambda_i << L with lambda_i = v_n / (n_e <sigma_i v_e>); the fraction of neutrals ionized over a plasma of thickness L is 1 - exp(-L/lambda_i); in the textbook example 95 % ionization needs L of about 3 lambda_i, so lambda_i / L should be below about 0.33.
sizing_relations.applicability: xenon-derived; v_n and <sigma_i v_e> are propellant dependent
sizing_relations.transfer_note: For N2, N, O2, O the neutral speed and ionization rate differ from xenon; SRC-GK2008 p. 336 notes that propellants lighter than xenon need a longer ionization region (Eq. 7.2-19). The ratio must be evaluated with Vyovrinda's propellant and chemistry set (TBD).

lambda_i_over_L_textbook_example.definition: upper value of lambda_i / L in the textbook example (95 % of incident neutral flux ionized)

sizing_relations.relation: The physical channel depth of a dielectric-wall Hall thruster is the magnetized plasma thickness L plus the length needed to demagnetize the plasma at the anode (textbook illustration: depth nearly twice the magnetized plasma length).

Across existing (xenon) Hall thrusters the channel width h is proportional to the mean diameter d, with a similar d/h ratio over a broad power range; the proportionality coefficient is not published in the source.
sizing_relations.locator: p. 241 (Fig. 2, Fig. 3 and text); p. 242 (coefficients not given)
sizing_relations.transfer_note: No air-species database; transfer is a hypothesis.

sizing_relations.relation: Mass flow m_dot = n_n m_n v_n pi d h; a critical atom density n_n,c keeps xenon Hall thrusters efficient, hence h d scales with the anode mass flow at fixed n_n,c. For ABEP the anode flow is harvested (IF-A5 mdot_anode_s_kgps, TBD), so this links the channel area to the delivered flow.
sizing_relations.locator: SRC-DM2008 Eq. (2.7), p. 7 and Sec. 4.2, p. 13; SRC-DM2011 p. 241 (critical density, h d proportional to m_dot)
sizing_relations.applicability: xenon; SRC-DM2008 infers n_n assuming a propellant temperature of 800 K
sizing_relations.transfer_note: Whether a critical density exists for N2/air at a similar value is unverified.

critical_atom_density_xenon.definition: critical propellant atom density inside the channel found for the xenon database
critical_atom_density_xenon.locator: SRC-DM2011 p. 241; SRC-DM2008 p. 13 (from Eq. 2.7 at normal operating flow, 800 K assumed)

sizing_relations.relation: Input power scales linearly with the product h d: P = C_P h d (xenon database).
sizing_relations.transfer_note: The coefficients are xenon values; for air species they are not established. Listed as evidence only.

C_P_analytic_xenon.definition: analytic proportionality coefficient of P = C_P h d (xenon)

C_P_empirical_xenon.definition: empirical proportionality coefficient of P = C_P h d (slope of Fig. 9, xenon)

sizing_relations.relation: SPT-family scaling (Daren et al., as summarized by the textbook): power, thrust, discharge current and mass flow scale with R^2 at constant inner-to-outer diameter ratio and constant lambda_i / L; the optimum current density is about constant with size.
sizing_relations.transfer_note: Xenon current densities; not transferable to air species without evidence.

sizing_relations.relation: Xenon SPT family by slot (outer channel) diameter: SPT-50 delivers thrust inside the RFP band at a few hundred watts; transfer of this size to air species is not implied.
sizing_relations.quantity_type: measured (flight data as tabulated in a textbook)
sizing_relations.transfer_note: Air species give a lower thrust per unit jet power at the same voltage for the same efficiency (see the ideal-beam table), and published light-propellant efficiencies are lower than xenon's (SRC-AFG2022 pp. 23-28).

sizing_relations.relation: Flight Hall channels are typically boron nitride or borosil (BN-SiO2), laboratory channels sometimes alumina; the pinned solver provides WallSheath materials Alumina, BoronNitride, SiliconDioxide, BNSiO2 and SiliconCarbide; the atmospheric-propellant ECHT used boron nitride of unstated grade and an extended channel to compensate for the lower residence time and ionization cross-section of light neutrals.
sizing_relations.locator: SRC-GK2008 p. 325; HallThruster.jl src/physics/wall_losses.jl lines 114-123; ECHT audit README 'What is available'; SRC-AFG2022 p. 26
sizing_relations.applicability: material and channel-length choices; no values adopted

bfield_interface.description: Radial magnetic field on the channel centreline B(z) of Vyovrinda's own magnetic circuit, in one of the two shape families the bridge already supports. All values TBD until a Vyovrinda magnetic-circuit computation or measurement exists.

measured_or_computed_profile.description: Tabulated centreline B(z) (CSV of z_mm, B_G with '#' comments and one header line) placed on the model axis by a rigid registration (never stretched) and scaled so that B at the exit plane or its maximum equals B_ref_T.
measured_or_computed_profile.limitations: Centreline radial field only (the 1-D solver has no field-line curvature). The solver holds B constant beyond the ends of the data, so the profile must span the whole domain.

asymmetric_gaussian_exit_peaked.description: Analytic B(z) = B_max exp(-((z - L)/sigma)^2) with sigma = sigma_in for z <= L and sigma_out beyond, peaking at the exit plane by construction.
asymmetric_gaussian_exit_peaked.limitations: Peak fixed at z = L; cannot represent plateau-shaped or upstream-peaked fields (the ECHT centreline field is a plateau, EV-B6). Admissible only if the Vyovrinda field is shown to match it within a tolerance the owner sets.

bridge_compatibility_rules: Use only the two shape families the bridge implements (bridge_lib.jl measured_bfield, bfield_gaussian); a new family is a bridge change reviewed on its own.
Registration is rigid (shift only, no stretching), as in measured_bfield.
The profile must cover z in [0, domain_length_m]: HallThruster.jl holds B constant beyond the ends of the data (bridge_lib.jl comment above measured_bfield).
Amplitude changes go through B_ref_T with solver_magnetic_field_scale = 1.0.
B_max_T, B_peak_minus_exit_m and B_scale reported by the bridge are recorded with every run.
Calibration-nuisance keys (p5_registration, p5_coil_shape) are never Vyovrinda field variables.

design_evidence.relation: In dielectric-wall Hall thrusters the centreline radial field peaks near the channel exit and is designed to be essentially zero at or near the anode.
Electrons magnetized, ions not: r_Le << L << r_Li, with r_e = (1/B) sqrt(8 m T_eV / (pi e)) and r_i = (1/B) sqrt(2 M V_b / e); electron Hall parameter squared >> 1.
design_evidence.applicability: any Hall channel; the textbook examples are xenon
design_evidence.transfer_note: r_i scales with sqrt(M): the ion Larmor-radius margin is smaller for N+, O+, N2+ than for Xe+ at the same B and V_b; to be checked with the Vyovrinda L and B_max (TBD).

r_e_example.definition: textbook example electron Larmor radius at T_e = 25 eV, B = 150 G

r_i_example_xenon.definition: textbook example xenon ion Larmor radius at 150 G and 300 eV

design_evidence.relation: Scaling of the field strength: B proportional to 1/(h d) from electron confinement (SRC-DM2008 Eq. 2.15); B proportional to m_dot/(h d) and to 1/L, and with the low-assumption set B proportional to sqrt(U_d) m_dot/(h d) and to sqrt(U_d)/L (SRC-DM2011 Eqs. 44-45): the field has to rise with discharge voltage and flow for a given geometry.
The xenon database thrusters operate with a field strength of typically about 200 G whatever the input power (consequence of operating near the critical atom density).
design_evidence.transfer_note: Not a Vyovrinda value; N2/air field requirements are unestablished.

typical_field_xenon_database.definition: typical maximum radial field of the xenon database thrusters

design_evidence.relation: The axial gradient matters: a radial field decreasing toward the anode gives higher efficiency; in xenon thrusters optimized for high efficiency the optimal field was found proportional to the discharge voltage (Hofer, as cited by the textbook). Field-line curvature near the exit (ion lens) also matters but is outside a 1-D centreline model.
design_evidence.locator: p. 329 (ion lens), p. 333 (optimal B proportional to V_d), p. 335 (gradient toward the anode)
design_evidence.applicability: xenon; transfer to air species unverified

design_evidence.relation: Field shapes differ between designs: the measured ECHT centreline field is a flat plateau (about 4.7 to 8.6 cm on its axis), not exit-peaked; the interface therefore must accept an arbitrary measured or computed profile.
design_evidence.applicability: ECHT only; evidence that shape families must be general, never a Vyovrinda field

discharge_voltage_interface.description: Discharge voltage V_d between anode and cathode common. One voltage set is shared by all three arms (INV-V1). The range and set below are PROPOSED for the owner; neither is in the RFP.
discharge_voltage_interface.supply_definition: Discharge supply between the anode (at the bottom of the channel) and cathode common; the thruster floats with respect to spacecraft common, and the beam voltage is V_d minus the cathode coupling voltage (SRC-GK2008 Eqs. (7.2-21) and (7.2-22), pp. 337-339, Fig. 7-7). In the 1-D solver, V_d is Config.discharge_voltage (bridge case Vd) and the cathode-side potential is Config.cathode_coupling_voltage.

proposed_range_V.definition: PROPOSED discharge-voltage range for the architecture comparison (common to all arms)
proposed_range_V.locator: span rule VR-1 (span_rule): span of span_voltages_V over literature_operating_points with span_role 'span_defining': lowest 180 V (ECHT, measured thrust), highest 350 V (BHT on air simulant, anodic efficiency 27 %)
proposed_range_V.rationale: Under span rule VR-1 it is the span of discharge voltages at which Hall-channel devices fed with air species (no xenon admixture) had a measured thrust reported in the open sources consulted (180-350 V). The unfiltered span of all reported Hall-channel air-species voltages is '<100' to 350 V (Dukhopelnikov et al. sweep with estimated thrust, recorded and excluded under VR-1(c)); the cusped-field MCFT-2139 (30-2000 V) is recorded and excluded under VR-1(a). VR-1 was stated at repair, not pre-declared (span_rule.provenance_of_rule). The range lies inside the 200-500 V tested range of the xenon SPT family except its 180 V end. Tie to the RFP envelope (ideal_beam_reference_table, model-derived identities only): at the 25 mN upper thrust end an ideal singly charged beam over this range needs a jet power of 0.412 kW (O2+, 180 V) to 0.868 kW (N+, 350 V), i.e. 27.5-57.9 % of the 1.5 kW ceiling before any efficiency loss or cathode, magnet and pre-ionizer power; published light-propellant anodic efficiencies are far below 1 (HT5k 8-18 %, BHT about 27 % (EV-V2), ECHT 13-23 %; SRC-AFG2022 pp. 25-26), so the ceiling is tight across the whole range. The envelope relations ER-1 to ER-6 show that the best V_d is not fixed a priori: at fixed efficiencies the jet-power cost of a given thrust rises as sqrt(V_d) (the <1.5 kW ceiling favours low V_d), the harvested flow sets a floor on V_d, and published light-propellant data show efficiency improving with voltage. Choosing a point would need an admitted closure or hardware; the range is therefore the filtered evidence span, not an optimum. The superseded 0-D grid (225-325 V) is not reused.

envelope_relations.relation: Anode efficiency eta_a = T^2 / (2 m_dot_a P_d), hence P_d = T v_eff / (2 eta_a) with v_eff = T / m_dot_a.

T = gamma sqrt(2M/e) I_b sqrt(V_b) with eta_v = V_b / V_d and mass utilization eta_m = m_dot_i / m_dot_a give, for one singly charged species, v_eff = gamma eta_m sqrt(2 e eta_v V_d / M) (our algebra from the cited equations).
envelope_relations.applicability: single species, singly charged; gamma lumps divergence and multiply charged ions

envelope_relations.relation: Thruster input power P_in = P_d + P_k + P_mag (discharge, keeper, magnet); in bus_power_boundary_v1 these are hall_discharge, cathode_keeper and hall_magnet, plus cathode_heater at start-up and rf_source or ecr_source + ecr_magnet in their arms. The RFP ceiling applies to the bus total as the bus-boundary lane accounts it.

From ER-1 and ER-2: at fixed thrust and fixed gamma, eta_m, eta_v and eta_a, P_d scales as sqrt(V_d) (and as 1/sqrt(M)); with the power ceiling this favours the low end of the voltage range. The ideal-beam table shows the scaling.
envelope_relations.applicability: holds only while the efficiencies stay fixed, which is not established (ER-6)

envelope_relations.relation: From ER-2: at fixed thrust T and harvested anode flow m_dot_a, V_d >= (M / (2 e eta_v)) (T / (gamma eta_m m_dot_a))^2; the intake-delivered flow (IF-A5, TBD) therefore sets a floor on V_d that rises as the flow falls.
envelope_relations.applicability: needs m_dot_a from the upstream chain and gamma, eta_m, eta_v from an admitted closure or hardware (all TBD)

envelope_relations.relation: Published light-propellant data show efficiency improving with voltage in some devices (EV-V1, EV-V2), which opposes ER-4; the optimum V_d is closure- and hardware-dependent (TBD), so the proposed range covers the filtered evidence span (VR-1) instead of a single point.

cathode_interface.description: Cathode of the common Hall accelerator: identical in all arms (INV-C1, INV-C2). Emitter and gas are PROPOSED from the lane brief and RFP context; every performance or design value is TBD pending the cathode lane.

cathode_type.definition: cathode type supplying discharge electrons and beam neutralization
cathode_type.rationale: Hall thrusters use an external hollow cathode as both discharge electron source and neutralizer (SRC-GK2008 pp. 327-328); owner confirms.

emitter_material.rationale: Lane brief (Xe-fed LaB6 per the RFP context 'air + Xe'; verify against the RFP text); the repository cathode model is LaB6 (abep_sim/plasma_devices.py LaB6Cathode, superseded 0-D context). LaB6 tolerates gas-feed impurities and air exposure better than BaO dispenser cathodes (SRC-GK2008 p. 255), which matters with ABEP backflow; the cathode lane owns the evidence.

feed_gas.rationale: RFP context 'air + Xe' (CLAUDE.md); the upstream ICD carries a Xe cathode flow at IF-X2. Published light-propellant Hall tests mostly fed the cathode with xenon (PPS1350-TSD campaign p. 23, Z-70 p. 26, Dukhopelnikov et al. p. 26, MCFT-2139 and HHT p. 27 of SRC-AFG2022), but not always: the shielded HT5k transitioned its HC20 cathode from xenon to pure N2 (p. 25) and the ECHT used an argon-fed cathode (p. 26; EV-C6). Xe is proposed from the RFP context, not because the literature is uniform.

evidence.relation: The external hollow cathode supplies the discharge electrons and neutralizes the beam; the discharge current is essentially the cathode electron emission current.
evidence.applicability: Hall thrusters with a hollow cathode

evidence.relation: The heater is turned off once the discharge is on (self-heating cathode); the keeper is normally used only during start-up and turned off after ignition, so keeper power is normally zero in operation.
evidence.applicability: xenon Hall thrusters; ABEP backflow may change the keeper need (cathode lane)

evidence.relation: The coupling voltage is typically of order 20 V, about 5 % to 10 % of the discharge voltage for moderate-Isp Hall thrusters.

typical_coupling_fraction_of_Vd.definition: typical coupling voltage as a fraction of V_d (moderate Isp)

evidence.relation: Cathode gas is injected outside the ionization region and is largely lost; cathode efficiency eta_c = m_dot_a / (m_dot_a + m_dot_c).

LaB6 cathodes are insensitive to impurities and air exposures that destroy BaO dispenser cathodes and withstand gas-feed impurity levels two orders of magnitude higher at the same emission current density; their life is set mainly by LaB6 evaporation. Poisoning is treated in the textbook's section 6.8.5.
evidence.applicability: LaB6 hollow cathodes (xenon operation); ABEP oxygen backflow to be quantified by the cathode lane

evidence.relation: In most published light-propellant Hall tests the cathode was supplied with xenon (PPS1350-TSD campaign p. 23; Z-70 and Dukhopelnikov et al. p. 26; MCFT-2139 and HHT p. 27), but not in all: one magnetically shielded HT5k test transitioned a centrally mounted HC20 hollow cathode from xenon to pure N2 (p. 25), and the ECHT used an argon-fed cathode (p. 26).
evidence.locator: SRC-AFG2022 pp. 23, 25, 26, 27; ECHT audit README (facility bullet)

evidence.relation: Hall thruster life is usually on the order of 10,000 h (xenon); ion sputter erosion of the dielectric walls near the exit ultimately determines life, and optimal exit-region magnetic design reduces wall bombardment.
evidence.locator: p. 325 (life order), p. 327 (wall erosion), p. 336 (magnetic design)

evidence.relation: PPS1350 500-h endurance attempt on N2/O2 with 10 % xenon at 305 V: about 314 h of steady operation, then anode oxidation produced anomalous behaviour and flame-outs; the authors judged the ceramic erosion compatible with a 7000-9500 h lifetime.

injection_interface.description: Where and in what form the pre-ionizer output enters the common Hall accelerator. The Hall reference requires the fields below at HALL_INLET_Z0; the interstage lane produces them. For hall_only the same plane receives the delivered neutral feed.

plane.location: anode / gas-distributor plane at the upstream end of the discharge channel
plane.coordinate: z = 0 of the Hall 1-D domain (anode face), same coordinate as geometry_interface
plane.notes: The cathode flow does not cross this plane. The pre-ionizer volume and its hardware are upstream of it and outside this reference.

applies_to.hall_only: Neutral-only inlet state: neutral fields equal the delivered anode feed (IF-A5 / IF-X2 anode flows at the gas-distributor thermal state); every ion and electron field is exactly zero by definition of the arm.
applies_to.rf_hall: Inlet state produced by the RF pre-ionizer (interstage lane): neutral, ion (per species and charge state) and electron fields; bus component rf_source.
applies_to.ecr_hall: Inlet state produced by the ECR pre-ionizer (interstage lane): neutral, ion (per species and charge state) and electron fields; bus components ecr_source and ecr_magnet (its field inside the Hall channel is constrained by INV-B3).

representation.definition: how the inlet state is represented
representation.value: moments_v1: per neutral species (mass flow, temperature, mean axial velocity, internal-state fractions) and per ion species and charge state (current, mean axial velocity, axial temperature), plus electron current, electron temperature and plasma potential relative to the anode; an optional tabulated axial velocity distribution may accompany any ion entry
representation.locator: HallThruster.jl heavy species are fluids (density, momentum; isothermal ions): src/simulation/heavy_species_update.jl apply_left_boundary!
representation.rationale: A drifting-Maxwellian moment set is what a fluid inflow condition of the 1-D solver would need; a tabulated distribution is kept optional for kinetic consumers. Owner and interstage lane to confirm.

mdot_neutral_kgps.definition: neutral mass flow crossing HALL_INLET_Z0 toward the exit, per species (e.g. N2, N, O2, O, Xe)
mdot_neutral_kgps.hall_only_rule: equals the delivered anode flow per species (IF-A5 mdot_anode_s_kgps, IF-X2 mdot_xe_anode_kgps)
mdot_neutral_kgps.solver_locator: Propellant flow_rate_kg_s (src/physics/gas.jl lines 356-364); the bridge wires one propellant per case (N2 through propellant_config, or one c.gas), so atomic N or mixed feeds are not wired
mdot_neutral_kgps.interstage_field: interstage_v1 result.neutrals[<species>].to_hall_flow_s [s^-1] x Species.mass -> kg s^-1

T_neutral_K.solver_locator: Propellant temperature_K (src/physics/gas.jl lines 372-377, 399-434); not passed by bridge_lib.jl run_case
T_neutral_K.interstage_field: interstage_v1 (18d2bfb) SourceExitState.neutral_temperature (one value; interstage assumes isothermal walls at it, so it is also a source-exit value carried to the inlet by assumption)

u_neutral_axial_m_s.definition: mean axial neutral velocity at HALL_INLET_Z0 (positive toward the exit)
u_neutral_axial_m_s.hall_only_rule: gas-distributor state (TBD); the solver derives it from temperature_K by a one-sided Maxwellian flux approximation when only the temperature is given
u_neutral_axial_m_s.solver_locator: Propellant velocity_m_s (src/physics/gas.jl lines 366-371, 416-422); not passed by bridge_lib.jl run_case
u_neutral_axial_m_s.interstage_field: not provided by interstage_v1 (free-molecular conductance model) — TBD — requires the interstage lane

neutral_internal_state.definition: fractions of vibrationally or electronically excited neutrals (and their levels) at HALL_INLET_Z0
neutral_internal_state.hall_only_rule: thermal equilibrium at the gas-distributor temperature (assumed; TBD)
neutral_internal_state.solver_locator: heavy_species_update.jl line 337 ('Anode flow feeds the ground state only') and line 422 ('Excited states have no anode inflow')
neutral_internal_state.interstage_field: not provided by interstage_v1 — TBD — requires the interstage lane

ion_current_A.definition: ion current crossing HALL_INLET_Z0 toward the exit, per ion species and charge state (e.g. N2+, N+, N2+ doubly charged, O+, Xe+)
ion_current_A.solver_locator: heavy_species_update.jl apply_left_boundary! lines 303-420: positive ions leave through the anode at the (sheath-corrected) Bohm speed and their flux is returned as ground-state neutrals (line 395); no ion inflow
ion_current_A.interstage_field: interstage_v1 result.ions[<ion species>].delivered_to_hall_flow_s [s^-1] x charge x e (interstage ion species carry their charge); fractions in result.charge_state_fractions.delivered

u_ion_axial_m_s.definition: mean axial ion velocity at HALL_INLET_Z0 (positive toward the exit)
u_ion_axial_m_s.solver_locator: heavy_species_update.jl apply_left_boundary! (ion boundary velocity fixed toward the anode)
u_ion_axial_m_s.interstage_field: interstage_v1 result.ions[<ion species>].axial_speed_m_s (constant along the duct: interstage assumption)

T_ion_axial_eV.definition: axial ion temperature (velocity spread about u_ion_axial_m_s) at HALL_INLET_Z0
T_ion_axial_eV.solver_locator: Propellant ion_temperature_K (src/physics/gas.jl lines 378-381) is a single isothermal-ion parameter used in the anode Bohm condition, not an inflow temperature
T_ion_axial_eV.interstage_field: not provided by interstage_v1 — TBD — requires the interstage lane

ion_velocity_distribution_ref.definition: optional repository path and sha256 of a tabulated axial velocity (or energy) distribution for the ion entry
ion_velocity_distribution_ref.interstage_field: not provided by interstage_v1 — TBD — requires the interstage lane

electron_current_A.definition: net electron current crossing HALL_INLET_Z0 from the pre-ionizer into the channel (sign: positive toward the exit)
electron_current_A.solver_locator: Config has no anode-plane electron injection (src/simulation/configuration.jl lines 54-200); electron boundaries are the anode sheath and the cathode boundary (cathode_Tev, cathode_coupling_voltage)
electron_current_A.interstage_field: not provided by interstage_v1 as a field (it gates a charge residual) — TBD — requires the interstage lane

T_e_inlet_eV.definition: electron temperature of the injected plasma at HALL_INLET_Z0
T_e_inlet_eV.solver_locator: anode_boundary_condition / anode_Tev (configuration.jl lines 78-90) are closure settings of the anode boundary, identical in all arms (INV-C2), not an injected state
T_e_inlet_eV.interstage_field: SOURCE-EXIT value, not an inlet-plane value: interstage_v1 (18d2bfb) takes SourceExitState.electron_temperature and holds it constant along the duct by its isothermal electron closure ('isothermal_source_conduction', an interstage assumption; ASSUMPTIONS in abep_sim/interstage.py). It does not compute the electron temperature at HALL_INLET_Z0; a T_e drop across the duct or the junction is not represented. Provisional mapping only (PENDING).

plasma_potential_rel_anode_V.definition: plasma potential of the injected plasma relative to the Hall anode; ions arriving below anode potential meet a retarding potential
plasma_potential_rel_anode_V.solver_locator: the solver computes its own anode sheath potential (anode_boundary_condition :sheath, heavy_species_update.jl lines 342-356)
plasma_potential_rel_anode_V.interstage_field: not provided by interstage_v1 — TBD — requires the interstage lane and the pre-ionizer electrical design

annular_nonuniformity.definition: azimuthal and radial non-uniformity of the injected flux across the annulus (definition to be fixed with the experiment protocol)
annular_nonuniformity.solver_locator: 1-D solver is radially and azimuthally averaged; the field is required for hardware comparisons
annular_nonuniformity.interstage_field: not provided by interstage_v1 (quasi-1-D) — TBD — requires the interstage lane and the experiment protocol

injected_flux_oscillation.definition: relative RMS and dominant frequency of the injected ion flux (coupling to Hall breathing oscillations)
injected_flux_oscillation.hall_only_rule: not applicable (steady neutral feed assumed; TBD)
injected_flux_oscillation.solver_locator: Propellant flow_rate_kg_s is constant in time
injected_flux_oscillation.interstage_field: not provided by interstage_v1 (steady) — TBD — requires the interstage lane

element_mass_flow_kgps.definition: mass flow per chemical element (N, O, Xe) summed over neutrals and ions at HALL_INLET_Z0; bookkeeping for the conservation gate
element_mass_flow_kgps.hall_only_rule: equals the delivered anode flow per element
element_mass_flow_kgps.solver_locator: bookkeeping field, not a solver input
element_mass_flow_kgps.interstage_field: derivable from interstage_v1 delivered ion and neutral flows x Species.composition and mass; interstage gates element residuals (result conservation.elements_rel)

conservation_rules: CR-1 element mass: for every element (N, O, Xe), the mass flow through HALL_INLET_Z0 (neutrals + ions) equals the anode flow delivered at IF-A5 / IF-X2 minus pre-ionizer losses that leave the system, each loss reported explicitly; the balance closes exactly (CLAUDE.md rule 4).

CR-2 charge: any net ion or electron current crossing HALL_INLET_Z0 appears in the circuit accounting of the pre-ionizer supply and the discharge supply (bus-boundary lane); injected charge is not free.

CR-3 energy: ionization, dissociation, excitation and heating carried across HALL_INLET_Z0 are paid by rf_source or ecr_source power in the bus ledger; the architecture energy-ledger residual stays below 2 % (CLAUDE.md rule 4).
CR-4 the cathode flow (IF-X2 mdot_xe_cathode_kgps, or IF-A5 mdot_cathode_air_kgps if an air-fed cathode is ever chosen) never crosses HALL_INLET_Z0.
CR-5 hall_only: the inlet state equals the delivered neutral feed; ion and electron fields are exactly zero.

findings.relation: Positive ions at the anode boundary are given a velocity toward the anode at the (sheath-corrected) Bohm speed, and the outflowing ion flux is sent back as ground-state neutrals: there is no ion inflow through the anode plane.
Anode flow feeds only the ground-state neutral fluid; excited states have no anode inflow.
Per-propellant neutral velocity and temperature (axial profiles) and an ion temperature exist in Propellant, but the bridge passes only the flow rate.
findings.applicability: pinned HallThruster.jl v0.23.1 and the current bridge

findings.relation: The only user hook for extra heavy-species sources is Config.source_heavy_species (default returns zero); representing injected ions through it, or changing the anode boundary, is a model change.
The bridge builds one propellant per case, so a mixed anode feed (air species plus xenon topping) is not representable today.

solver_capability.consequence: rf_hall and ecr_hall cannot be evaluated through the pinned Hall model today, and their Hall maps must be refused (not run with the pre-ionization dropped; SRC-HALLMAP-SPEC section 12). Closing the gap is an owner-approved model change with its own validation plan. It is applied identically to all three arms, and with every injected ion and electron field at zero it must reproduce the pinned hall_only result (INV-S1). The HallThruster.jl pin is never moved automatically (PINNED.toml upgrade_policy).
